solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Jail troops involved in criminal blast (7)

indicators.note: the troops are caught up inside the other letters
a criminal blast is a crooked, rearranged one

annotation.surface: Soldiers caught up in a criminal bombing end up behind bars.
annotation.walkthrough: A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders, abolished in 1982. The explosion in the surface is only letters to shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly loose: the institution locked up young offenders rather than adults.

entries.clue: Voluntary pilot on manoeuvres round America (8)

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, as these letters do
the rearranged letters go round the A

annotation.surface: A volunteer pilot flies exercises over America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like part of 'on manoeuvres' alone, but it is fodder too: PILOT ON supplies seven of the eight letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe what you may choose to do but need not.

entries.clue: Quiet walks in abattoir (8)

annotation.surface: Someone strolls quietly through a slaughterhouse.
annotation.walkthrough: A shambles was originally a meat market or slaughterhouse; the modern sense of a mess grew out of that bloody scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Shambles is an old word for a slaughterhouse or butchers' market.

entries.clue: Behind former leading lady’s own fragrance (10)

blocks.note: aft = behind, at the back of a ship
ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen, plus the 's

annotation.surface: An actress who once starred has a signature scent of her own.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests the theatre, but here it is the late Queen, ER; 'former' marks that her reign is over.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the scented lotion men splash on after a shave is one kind of fragrance.

entries.clue: Face nuisance in hearing (4)

indicators.note: we are told how the word sounds, not how it is spelt

annotation.surface: Someone has to confront an annoyance at a tribunal hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: A pane is a flat side or face, as of a nut, a bolt head or a cut gem, not only a sheet of glass.
annotation.definitionFit: A pane can be one flat face of a many-sided object.

entries.clue: Mum meets her mate, an inactive investor (6,7)

blocks.note: mum = saying nothing, as in 'keep mum'

annotation.surface: A mother is introduced to her husband, who turns out to be a hands-off investor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother but the adjective meaning quiet. A silent partner puts money into a business without running it.
annotation.definitionFit: A silent partner invests in a firm but takes no active part in it.

entries.clue: See 6
Rector originally means to leave for retreat (7)

indicators.note: take what the rector is at the start: his first letter

blocks.note: an egress is a way out

annotation.surface: A vicar plans to leave for a spiritual retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like a religious getaway to suit the rector, but it is the verb: to go backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to go backwards, to a former place or state.

entries.clue: Check ladies perhaps coming around, I see (8)

indicators.note: something coming around turns to face the other way, so the word is read back to front
the ladies are one example of a lavatory

blocks.note: LAV, a lavatory such as the ladies, turned round
to see someone = to date them

annotation.surface: Someone checks on some women visiting, and says they understand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The ladies' is a British name for a women's toilet, hence LAV. 'I see' reads as 'I understand' but splits into I and a verb for courting.
annotation.definitionFit: To validate is to check and confirm something is correct.

entries.clue: Slyness of way wife’s abandoned riches (7)

indicators.note: the wife has left, so W comes out of the word

annotation.surface: A cunning wife has walked out on her husband's fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wife's' is 'wife has', so the wife is what goes missing from the riches.
annotation.definitionFit: Stealth is secretive, sly behaviour.

entries.clue: Home counties expert leaving India for time to study (8)

indicators.note: India departs from the word, so I comes out

blocks.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England
MEISTER, an expert, without I (India in the radio alphabet)

annotation.surface: A specialist from near London goes to India for a spell of study.
annotation.walkthrough: A meister is a borrowed German word for an expert, as in 'quizmeister'. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
annotation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year term of study.

entries.clue: Free programs divide China? (9)

blocks.note: china is one kind of ware, pottery; the question mark flags the example

annotation.surface: A question of whether free software could split the Chinese nation.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C disguises china the crockery as China the country.
annotation.definitionFit: Shareware is software handed out free to try.

entries.clue: One taking medal carried by posh car around Belgium (6)

indicators.note: the medal rides inside the car
the medal wraps round Belgium

blocks.note: OBE = Order of the British Empire, split O…BE

annotation.surface: A medal winner rides off in a luxury car touring Belgium.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One taking medal' looks like a winner at a ceremony; the definition stops at 'One taking', a thief.
annotation.definitionFit: A robber is one who takes what is not theirs.

entries.clue: Maybe Mimi appears for the audience with a lock of hair (10)

indicators.note: an audience hears the word, so we go by its sound

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair

annotation.surface: An opera heroine takes the stage with a curl of hair.
annotation.walkthrough: Mimi, heroine of Puccini's La Bohème, is a seamstress. The opera setting makes 'audience' feel natural.
annotation.definitionFit: Mimi in La Bohème sews for a living.

entries.clue: Leader with vast organised forced labour movement (5,5)

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

annotation.surface: A trade-union leader with a huge organised following heads a labour movement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Labour movement' reads as the trade unions, but the movement is the physical shipping of enslaved people.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic twist on a common phrase: the traffic shipped captives across oceans, a movement of people into forced labour.

entries.clue: Look, part of Suez agreement needs overturning (4)

indicators.note: the answer is a piece of the following words
that piece reads backwards

blocks.note: suEZ AGreement: four letters spanning the two words, to be read backwards

annotation.surface: A demand that the Suez treaty be overturned.
annotation.walkthrough: The Suez Crisis of 1956 gives the surface its politics.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a noun or verb: a steady stare.

entries.clue: Agents had redeployed theatre worker (5,4)

indicators.note: the letters are deployed again in new positions

annotation.surface: Spies were moved to work undercover backstage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Agents' suggests theatrical agents to go with the stage, but the word only lends its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A stagehand moves scenery and props in a theatre.

entries.clue: Old Republican in party beginning to notice trouble, one perhaps getting hammered (8)

indicators.note: only the start of 'notice' is used

annotation.surface: An elderly Republican politician at a party gets drunk and causes trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' suggests drunk at the party, but a doornail is a big nail hammered into a door. 'In' only puts the Republican at the party, so the letters follow DO.
annotation.definitionFit: A doornail is a stud hammered into a door, as in 'dead as a doornail'.

entries.clue: Some glass ain’t even broken (8)

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, naming a kind of glass

indicators.note: broken glass lies in pieces, and so do the letters

annotation.surface: A piece of glass that isn't even cracked.
annotation.walkthrough: Venetian glass is the fine glassware made on Murano, near Venice.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the fine glassware of Murano is one variety, so the adjective picks out some glass.

entries.clue: Goddess representing fish (7)

annotation.surface: A goddess depicted as a fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Representing' looks like 'depicting', but it is used as 'standing for', which gives FOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Roman deity of luck is one goddess among many.

entries.clue: Promise of upside-down cake kept by British hotel (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads from the bottom up
the cake is held between the other letters

blocks.note: TORTE, a rich cake, read upwards
H = hotel in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: A British hotel keeps an upside-down pudding on the menu.
annotation.walkthrough: The upside-down cake is a real dessert, which hides the instruction to turn the word over.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific sense: the verb means to promise someone in marriage.

entries.clue: Warning in exhortation to workers? (4)

blocks.note: O, the vocative cry of an address
men = workers, as in 'management and men'

annotation.surface: A foreman's rallying cry to the workforce carries a warning.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole phrase is the cry 'O men!', an appeal to the workforce.
annotation.definitionFit: An omen is a warning sign of what is to come.

entries.clue: Access passwords? (4,6)

blocks.note: the surface pushes a computer login; the setter means gaining entry to a place
not a secret string of characters but a magic formula spoken aloud at a door

annotation.surface: A computer user asks for their login details.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passwords' reads as a computer login, but the words that gain access are Ali Baba's two words to the robbers' cave.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Open sesame' are the words that give entry, and so any easy means of access.

entries.clue: Cross lake going for take-off (6)

indicators.note: the lake is going away, so L comes out

blocks.note: St Andrew's X-shaped cross, split SA…L…TIRE

annotation.surface: A plane crosses a lake on its way to take off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb or 'angry', but it is a noun: the saltire, the diagonal cross on Scotland's flag.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of mockery: a take-off sends someone up by imitation.

entries.clue: Half-cut man enthralled by bitter purpose (6)

indicators.note: half of the word is cut off
the man is held captive inside the other word

blocks.note: GENT, a man, with its second half cut

annotation.surface: A drunk man is captivated by a sour drink with a purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits a bitter, the beer; here it just halves GENT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the goal you aim at.

entries.clue: Flyer has time for second check (8)

indicators.note: the bird takes on a new letter
'for' in the sense 'in exchange for': time is swapped in where the second was

blocks.note: a throstle is a song thrush

annotation.surface: An airline passenger spends time on a second security check.
annotation.walkthrough: Throstle is an old word for the song thrush.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to choke off or hold back, as an engine's fuel is held back.

entries.clue: Hospital usher grasps sponge (4)

indicators.note: the words hold the answer in their grip

annotation.surface: A hospital porter picks up a sponge.
annotation.walkthrough: A sponge is a heavy drinker, one who soaks it up; so is a lush.
annotation.definitionFit: Both lush and sponge are slang for a drunkard.

entries.clue: Alarm about adult contracting onset of infectious disease (7)

indicators.note: the letters are moved about
only the start of 'infectious' is used

blocks.note: A = adult, as in film ratings

annotation.surface: Concern grows about a grown-up catching an infection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Infectious disease' reads as one phrase, but only 'disease' is the definition; infectious gives just its I.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the mosquito-borne fever is one disease among many.

entries.clue: Confirm implication of pay freeze? (8)

blocks.note: to certify a document formally, as a notary does
what a frozen salary tells you: three short words run together

annotation.surface: A worker asks whether the frozen pay means no increase.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT A RISE and it is exactly what a pay freeze means; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A notary confirms a document is genuine by notarising it.

entries.clue: Refuse to weaken (7)

blocks.note: to turn down an offer politely
as health or powers fail with age

annotation.surface: Someone will not give in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Refuse to weaken' reads as one stubborn phrase; split it before 'to' and each half is a sense of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Decline means both to turn down and to grow weaker.
